title: Google's New AI Note-Taking App Transcribes Meetings Entirely Offline
excerpt: AI Edge Foresight, an experimental Mac app built on EmbeddingGemma 2 and Gemma 4, keeps all audio and files on-device — a privacy pitch aimed at confidential meetings.
body:
• Google has released AI Edge Foresight, an experimental meeting-assistant app for Apple Silicon Macs that transcribes meetings completely offline — no internet connection or cloud subscription required.
  • Users jot bullet points during a meeting and Foresight expands them into detailed notes from the live transcript; it also detects questions and answers them in real time from a personal knowledge base of local files and Google Drive documents.
  • It runs on Google's new EmbeddingGemma 2 multimodal embedding model and the Gemma 4 language model, is free to download, and is open-sourced under Apache 2.0 as a showcase for developers.
  • What it means for you: if you handle confidential meetings, the pitch is privacy — nothing leaves your Mac — but it is experimental, and Google has not said whether non-English transcription works equally well.

Google has released an AI meeting assistant that works without an internet connection. Called AI Edge Foresight, the experimental Mac app captures your meetings, transcribes them and turns your rough bullet points into polished notes — all processed on the device itself, with nothing sent to the cloud.

What Foresight does

Foresight runs on Apple Silicon Macs and is free to download; initial setup takes about a minute to pull down the required on-device models. Because it captures microphone input and system audio directly, it works with any meeting platform, according to Google.

During a meeting, users jot brief bullet points and Foresight expands them into detailed notes using the ongoing transcript — hands-on testing found it "quickly and successfully turned my bullet points into notes." It also detects questions raised during the meeting and provides relevant answers in real time, searching a personal knowledge base of documents, images, transcripts and notes using natural language. Point the app at project folders, reference materials, diagrams and calendars — it supports local files and Google Drive — and Google says it "automatically understands your work without needing to manually organize your files." A multimodal search feature can locate a specific moment in hours of recordings from a text query, such as finding a particular voice memo clip.

Under the hood

Foresight is built on two new models: EmbeddingGemma 2, a multimodal embedding model from Google DeepMind, and the Gemma 4 language model. EmbeddingGemma 2 converts text, code, images, video frames and audio into numerical vectors in the same vector space, so similar material can be retrieved across formats — the trick that lets one model search transcripts, documents and recordings together.

The model is small by modern standards: 740 million parameters, needing about 191MB of active RAM for text-only weights or 567MB for the full multimodal model. Google says image processing — the most computationally demanding part of the workload — runs at 37.3 milliseconds per image on an M5 Pro's GPU, roughly 27 images per second. The whole stack is open-sourced under Apache 2.0, so developers can freely integrate it into their own apps. The company's stated design goal is to "organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware," with EmbeddingGemma 2 positioned as an "ultra-low-latency on-device decision engine" for privacy-first applications.

"Organize, search, and connect information directly on consumer hardware."

— Google, on the design goal behind AI Edge Foresight

Foresight joins AI Edge Gallery and AI Edge Eloquent — an offline transcription tool — in Google's family of Mac apps, with demos of the underlying technology also available in AI Edge Gallery on Android and iOS.

The privacy pitch

The headline selling point is that all transcript and audio processing takes place on the device. For anyone holding confidential meetings — lawyers, doctors, executives — that is a meaningful alternative to entrusting transcripts to a cloud service. It is also a deliberate move into territory Apple has long claimed: AI that runs locally and keeps all data on the device.

One thing Foresight is not: a replacement for Google Meet's "Take notes for me," the cloud-based Gemini feature that requires a Google AI Pro subscription at $19.99 a month or an eligible Workspace plan. That is a separate product. Foresight is free and offline — but also far less polished.

The caveats

Google is clear that this is an experimental developer showcase, not a flagship consumer launch. It has not said whether transcription works equally well for meetings held in languages other than English — though a companion AI Edge Gallery demo showed image search working with German search terms. For now, Foresight is best understood as a glimpse of where on-device AI is headed: assistants that know your work, answer your questions, and never phone home.
